name: COBRA
summary: COBRA developed room-temperature CdZnTe semiconductor arrays for double-beta-decay searches. Its Gran Sasso demonstrator tested low-background operation, pulse-shape selection and background control for a larger array.
detection_principle: The semiconductor is both source and calorimeter. Coplanar-grid electrodes measure deposited electron energy; pulse shapes distinguish surface backgrounds and different charge-collection topologies.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
